# Skein — full LLM context

Skein 0.5 is a tiny HTML-first Web Components runtime for creative websites and interactive documents. It adds fine-grained reactive state, keyed lists, conditions and scoped lifecycle while leaving rendering media native: HTML stays HTML, CSS stays CSS, SVG stays SVG, and Canvas stays imperative Canvas.

Production entry: `skein.min.js`.
Current production size: 13,988 B raw, 5,086 B gzip, 4,606 B Brotli.
Runtime dependencies: zero.
Repository: https://github.com/Pom4H/web-component
Website: https://pom4h.github.io/web-component/
Playground: https://pom4h.github.io/web-component/playground/

## Core philosophy

1. The browser is already the rendering engine. Do not introduce a virtual DOM.
2. Static content should remain static semantic HTML. Skein binds only dynamic data.
3. SEO-critical headings, links, product copy, article text, metadata and structured information should normally be present in the original HTML response.
4. Skein currently has no SSR or hydration. If request-time HTML is required, generate it outside Skein and enhance the result.
5. `{...}` contains property paths, not arbitrary JavaScript expressions.
6. Put derived logic in `computed()`.
7. Prefer native browser APIs over framework abstractions.
8. Keep the runtime and official examples zero-dependency unless a task explicitly chooses otherwise.

## Smallest app

```html
<click-count></click-count>

<template skein="click-count">
  <script>
    this.count = 0
    this.up = () => this.count++
  </script>

  <button @click={up}>clicked {count}</button>
</template>

<script type="module"
  src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/Pom4H/web-component@main/skein.min.js">
</script>
```

No npm, CLI, bundler, config file or application server is required.

## External component convention

Custom-element names map to HTML files by replacing hyphens with slashes:

```text
<counter-app> -> counter/app.html
<user-card>   -> user/card.html
```

A component source can contain top-level `<script>`, markup and `<style>` in one file.

## State

Component scripts execute with `this` bound to a deep reactive Proxy:

```js
this.count = 0
this.count++
this.user = { name: 'Ada' }
this.user.name = 'Grace'
this.items = []
this.items.push({ id: 1, title: 'One' })
```

Synchronous writes automatically settle in one scheduled microtask wave. Skein 0.5 has no public `batch()` helper.

Missing-property reads are reactive. Array length/structure is reactive, including direct truncation with `array.length = n`.

## Bindings

Text:

```html
<h1>Hello {user.name}</h1>
```

String attribute:

```html
<div title="User {user.name}"></div>
```

DOM property:

```html
<input .value={user.name}>
```

Boolean attribute:

```html
<button ?disabled={saving}>Save</button>
```

Event:

```html
<button @click={save}>Save</button>
```

Do not generate `onclick={save}` as a Skein binding. The v0.5 event syntax is `@event={handler}`.

Context:

```html
<address in={user.address}>
  {city}, {street}
</address>
```

Context lookup is lexical and walks outward to root component state. A present local property whose value is `undefined` still shadows an outer property.

## Lists

```html
<article for={projects} key={id}>
  <b>{index}. {title}</b>
  <input placeholder="DOM state survives reorder">
</article>
```

Use a stable unique key when records have application identity.

Without an explicit key:
- objects use object identity;
- primitive duplicates are disambiguated by occurrence.

List reconciliation is incremental:
- append creates only new views;
- removal disposes only removed views;
- reorder moves existing DOM nodes instead of recreating them;
- browser-local form state can survive reorder;
- `index` and `$index` are reactive locals.

Do not replace keyed lists with full `innerHTML` rerenders.

## Conditions

```html
<section if={inspectorOpen}>
  <canvas></canvas>
</section>
```

A conditional branch owns a child reactive scope. False disposes its effects, event listeners, nested components and DOM view; true instantiates a new scoped view.

## Computed values

```html
<script>
  this.price = 100
  this.quantity = 2
  this.total = computed(() => this.price * this.quantity)
</script>

<strong>{total}</strong>
```

Computed values are lazy, cached and dependency-tracked.

## Effects

```js
effect(() => {
  console.log(this.total)
})
```

Render work settles before user effects. If a user effect dirties rendering, render work runs again before later user effects.

## Component-script helpers

The injected helper surface is intentionally only:

- `computed(fn)` — lazy cached derived state.
- `effect(fn)` — user effect after render effects.
- `onCleanup(fn)` — deterministic cleanup owned by the current component scope.
- `host` — current Skein custom element.
- `abortSignal` — scope-owned native AbortSignal.

Removed/not public in v0.5: `batch`, `signal`, `untrack`.

Example cleanup:

```js
window.addEventListener('resize', this.measure, { signal: abortSignal })
fetch('/data.json', { signal: abortSignal })

const frame = requestAnimationFrame(this.draw)
onCleanup(() => cancelAnimationFrame(frame))
```

The AbortController is allocated lazily and only when `abortSignal` is actually used by a component script.

## Public module/global API

```js
Skein.version
Skein.define(tag, source)
```

`window.Skein` exposes the same object in the browser.

Do not rely on low-level runtime internals such as Scheduler, Signal, Effect, ReactiveState, `Skein.stats` or `Skein.flush`; they are not part of the v0.5 public contract.

## Lifecycle

Every component owns a root scope. Lists and branches create child scopes.

Disconnect pauses reactive effects. Reconnect resumes dirty work without rebuilding the current view. `connectedMoveCallback()` is supported where the browser uses state-preserving custom-element moves.

Permanent teardown is explicit:

```js
host.dispose()
```

Renderer-owned list/branch removal disposes automatically, including nested Skein custom elements.

## Static HTML and SEO

Skein has no SSR today. This does not mean page content should be generated in JavaScript.

Recommended page:

```html
<main>
  <h1>Creative websites with native HTML, CSS, SVG and Canvas.</h1>
  <p>Skein adds fine-grained reactive bindings without a virtual DOM.</p>
  <a href="/work/">See the work</a>
  <interactive-demo></interactive-demo>
</main>
```

The heading, paragraph and link already exist in the HTML response. Skein owns the interactive region.

If a server must compute personalized/request-dependent HTML, use an external server/static-generation layer.

## Creative CSS pattern

```html
<script>
  this.x = 50
  this.move = event => this.x = event.offsetX
</script>

<article style="--x:{x}px" @pointermove={move}>
  <h1>Skein</h1>
</article>

<style>
  h1 { transform: translateX(var(--x)); }
</style>
```

Use CSS for interpolation, transitions, layout and keyframes.

## SVG pattern

```html
<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100">
  <circle cx={x} cy={y} r="4" />
</svg>
```

Keep the SVG tree native. Skein should update only dynamic attributes/properties.

## Canvas pattern

Canvas should retain an imperative render loop. Use Skein for state, controls and cleanup:

```html
<script>
  let frame
  queueMicrotask(() => {
    const ctx = host.shadowRoot.querySelector('canvas').getContext('2d')
    const draw = () => {
      // ordinary Canvas rendering
      frame = requestAnimationFrame(draw)
    }
    draw()
  })
  onCleanup(() => cancelAnimationFrame(frame))
</script>

<canvas></canvas>
```

## Runtime architecture

Readable files:

```text
skein.js
runtime/reactive.js
runtime/template.js
runtime/component.js
```

`runtime/reactive.js` contains the dependency graph, computed values, scheduler, scopes, reactive Proxy and lexical binding lookup.

`runtime/template.js` compiles real DOM to compact instruction tuples and implements exact DOM bindings, keyed reconciliation and conditional branches.

`runtime/component.js` implements source loading/caching, registration, Custom Element lifecycle and script execution.

Important v0.5 implementation properties:
- binding paths compile once;
- ordinary lookup does not allocate frame arrays;
- list keys resolve directly against items;
- Scope resources and AbortController are lazy;
- declarative event cleanup does not allocate one AbortController per list item;
- production diagnostics counters are gone;
- renderer does not attach legacy `$`, `open` or `replace` properties to every DOM element;
- nested Skein elements are explicitly disposed with their owning view;
- disconnected instances are not permanently retained by the registration registry.

## Production build

`tools/build.mjs` is a zero-dependency Node bundler/minifier for the CDN file:

```bash
node tools/build.mjs
node tools/build.mjs --check
```

It concatenates the readable runtime, strips module-only syntax, lexically minifies and mangles known internal identifiers while preserving strings/regex literals.

The generated `skein.min.js` is tested directly in Chrome. Do not modify it by hand.

## Testing

```bash
node test/run.mjs
```

Requirements: Node.js 22+ and Chrome/Chromium.

The runner uses Node built-ins and raw Chrome DevTools Protocol. No Playwright, Puppeteer, jsdom, Jest or Vitest.

Coverage includes reactive core behavior, missing properties, array truncation, exact bindings, keyed identity, nested disposal, lifecycle/reconnect, CSS style parsing, production SVG/Canvas behavior, inline bootstrap, late registration in Shadow DOM, generated minified runtime correctness and Playground sandbox serialization.

## Current limitations

- no SSR or hydration;
- no built-in async resource/suspense primitive;
- no built-in error-boundary primitive;
- `{...}` expressions are property paths rather than arbitrary JavaScript;
- component scripts use `AsyncFunction`, so strict CSP currently requires `unsafe-eval`.

## Rules for AI agents

When building a Skein application:
1. Start with the smallest native HTML solution.
2. Keep semantic/SEO-critical content outside client-only components when it can be static.
3. Use Skein only where state/interactivity is useful.
4. Prefer one-file `<template skein>` for tiny examples.
5. Use external tag-to-path component files when a project grows.
6. Keep `{...}` to paths and use `computed()` for derivation.
7. Use `.property`, `?boolean` and `@event` bindings for their native semantics.
8. Use stable keys for persistent list identity.
9. Use CSS, SVG and Canvas directly.
10. Register resource cleanup with `onCleanup()` or `abortSignal`.
11. Do not add dependencies unless explicitly requested.
12. Do not reintroduce removed low-level/public compatibility APIs without an explicit requirement.

When modifying the runtime, read `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/skills/skein/references/architecture.md` first, regenerate `skein.min.js`, and run the full test suite.
